reasoning: The procedure's rule 'A shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery' governs this case directly. A row whose definition of done names his eye as the check is read as describing one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserve for him — a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a change to the definition of correct still standing as an open fork — never an ordinary buildable result that a command, a test, or a plain read already confirms was delivered. Here the delivered state is exactly that ordinary result: `scripts/render-board.sh` regenerates `board.html`, every row the plan declares appears under its own state, `tests/test_board_matches_the_canon.py` passes against the generated page, and the delivery explicitly holds no matter of preference — the page shows what the plan holds and nothing else. So the acceptance line's wording is superseded by what the work turned out to be, and the correct move is to run the acceptance receipt with a verifier who is not the row's own holder — and, because the done names a rendered surface (the words 'page' and 'board.html' trigger that refusal), the receipt must carry `--surface` pointing at the rendered page, since a fixture passing is not the surface rendering — then close the checkpoint and row in the same step and show the result. Nothing here is irreversible outside git, so rule 12's own ground does not stop the work for his word. That he has not looked is not a hold: the pipeline shows the result and continues without waiting for his attention, and if he disagrees afterward that disagreement is a new fact carrying its own task, not a reopening of the row that shipped.
